name: Ezekiel
lede: The twenty-sixth book of the Bible, in full: the visions of God by the river Chebar, the watchman of the house of Israel, the glory departing from the temple, the parables and the burdens of the nations, the valley of dry bones, and the house of the vision with the river flowing from under its threshold, every word in the words of the ASV.

books.name: The Visions of God
books.blurb: Among the captives by the river Chebar the heavens were opened: a stormy wind out of the north, the four living creatures, the wheels with their rims full of eyes, the firmament like the terrible crystal, and above it a throne of sapphire, fire and brightness — the appearance of the likeness of the glory of Jehovah; the roll of a book eaten, in the mouth as honey; and I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel.

books.name: The Siege on a Tile
books.blurb: Take thee a tile, and portray upon it a city, even Jerusalem: the forts and the mound and the iron pan; the prophet lying on his left side and on his right, each day for a year; the bread of the siege by weight; the hair shaven with a sword and divided in three; set thy face toward the mountains of Israel; and an end, the end is come upon the four corners of the land.

books.name: The Glory Departs
books.blurb: Lifted up between earth and heaven and brought in the visions of God to Jerusalem: the image of jealousy, the chamber of imagery and the seventy elders with their censers, the women weeping for Tammuz, the men worshipping the sun; the man clothed in linen and the mark upon the foreheads; coals of fire from between the cherubim; and the glory of Jehovah going up from the threshold to the east gate, and to the mountain east of the city.

books.name: Stuff for Removing
books.blurb: The prophet a sign: stuff for removing carried out by day, the wall digged through in the dark — I am your sign; the net spread for the prince in Jerusalem; bread eaten with quaking; the foolish prophets like foxes in the waste places, and the wall daubed with untempered mortar brought down by the stormy wind; and though these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it.

books.name: The Vine and the Foundling
books.blurb: What is the vine-tree more than any tree? — cast into the fire for fuel; then Jerusalem, cast out in the open field in the day that she was born, washed and clothed and decked with ornaments, who trusted in her beauty; her lovers and her judgment; Samaria and Sodom her sisters; and nevertheless I will remember my covenant with thee in the days of thy youth.

books.name: The Eagles and the Cedar
books.blurb: A riddle of two great eagles, the top of the cedar and the vine of low stature, and its meaning — the king that despised the oath; a tender twig planted upon the mountain of the height of Israel; the fathers have eaten sour grapes — the soul that sinneth, it shall die, and turn yourselves, and live; and a lamentation for the princes of Israel: the lioness and her whelps, and the vine plucked up in fury.
